pa:2611.18919.name: Correcting Persistent Failures in Point-Cloud Grasping Policies using Human Demonstrations in Virtual Reality
pa:2611.18919.desc: A human-in-the-loop failure-mining pipeline turns persistently unsolved grasps of a reinforcement-learning point-cloud policy into virtual-reality human demonstrations, improving hard-case success without reducing generalization to unseen objects.

pa:2611.16642.name: Dataset Distillation via Drifting
pa:2611.16642.desc: A dataset distillation method learns synthetic samples that approximate per-class data distributions in a feature extractor's latent space, improving distribution coverage and classification training while supporting visualization and other modalities.

pa:2611.21439.name: A Reinforcement Learning Method to Navigate SMEFT Operator Space
pa:2611.21439.desc: A reinforcement learning agent with a lightweight actor-critic architecture explores the Standard Model Effective Field Theory operator space to discover diverse high-quality theory hypotheses and improve global fits.

pa:2611.21072.name: Sage S2.1 Flash Technical Report
pa:2611.21072.desc: We introduce Sage S1.5 Flash, a 320-billion-parameter general-purpose mixture-of-experts model designed to reason over scientific evidence and act in interactive environments. Sage Sci-Perception uses dedicated encoders for molecular graphs and biological sequences and represents spectra as ordered patches of measurements. Modality-specific projectors map these representations into the input space
pa:2611.21072.zh: 能看懂科學數據與分子結構的超大型AI模型

pa:2611.17110.name: SALA: Semantically Aligned Latent Actions Enable Dual-Axis Scaling of Embodied Foundation Models
pa:2611.17110.desc: SALA aligns latent actions across human and robot videos by using language-based semantic similarities to form a shared latent action space that supervises embodied foundation model training and improves robot task performance.

pa:2611.17933.name: OutfitterBench: Evaluating LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Resource Allocation and Commitment Coordination
pa:2611.17933.desc: OutfitterBench evaluates LLM agents managing a 200-day outdoor-equipment rental business under fixed capital and uncertain demand, revealing limitations in sustaining feasible commitments and reallocating resources.

pa:2611.19537.name: Continuation-Guided LLM Evolution of Program Policies and Goal Compilers in Craftax
pa:2611.19537.desc: A framework uses coding agents and a feedback cascade to synthesize code-based policies that achieve long-horizon success and can be factored into a reusable goal compiler for zero-shot transfer to new tasks.

pa:2611.21218.name: InclusionMed: Benchmarking AI for Inclusive Healthcare
pa:2611.21218.desc: InclusionMed is an open medical AI evaluation initiative that audits and reproduces benchmarks across healthcare roles and capabilities, revealing that model rankings and inference costs vary by context and motivating broader, context-specific evaluation.
pa:2611.21218.zh: 全面檢測醫療AI在不同情境下表現的評測系統
pa:2611.21218.why: 揪出醫療AI在不同應用下的真實表現與成本差異，幫助醫療領域挑選最適合的AI工具

pa:2611.20148.name: Centered Ablation: Why Last-Layer Directional Ablation Under-Fires or Collapses, and a Closed-Form Fix
pa:2611.20148.desc: Directional ablation removes a hidden state's component along a "behaviour direction" while a language model runs. It is the standard way to switch a behaviour such as refusal off, but it is erratic: on some models it barely fires, on others the text collapses into repetition. We show why, and fix it. At the last residual stream, ablation is exactly a logit bias: a fixed vocabulary footprint scale

pa:2611.20218.name: SWE-CoWork: Benchmarking Coding Agents as Digital Employees in Organizations
pa:2611.20218.desc: A benchmark of realistic software engineering assignments reveals that current coding agents struggle to track requirements from clarification through implementation, verification, and handoff, completing few tasks despite partial test success.
pa:2611.20218.zh: 測試AI軟體工程師在真實公司環境的協作能力
pa:2611.20218.why: 用真實軟體開發任務測試發現，現今AI還無法完整搞定從需求確認到驗證的整個流程

pa:2611.20385.name: DominoBench: Evaluating Multi-Step Physical Reasoning from Still Images
pa:2611.20385.desc: A new benchmark, DominoBench, shows that current vision-language and multimodal models cannot reliably predict physical outcomes from still images unless the critical calculation and necessary quantities are provided.

pa:2605.09614.name: Reflection Anchors for Propagation-Aware Visual Retention in Long-Chain Multimodal Reasoning
pa:2605.09614.desc: Long chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning improves large vision--language models, but visual information often fades during generation, limiting long-horizon multimodal reasoning. pa:2611.20882.name: Accelerate Bench: Evaluating Agents for Application-Level Program Optimization
pa:2611.20882.desc: Application optimization requires coding agents to discover useful changes and coordinate them across a complete program while preserving the required computation. We introduce Accelerate Bench, a benchmark of 32 CPU optimization tasks adapted from scientific applications and supercomputing competitions. Each task provides a working program and specifies the workload, correctness requirements, tim

pa:2611.18668.name: UMM-JEPA: Generative Pretraining via Masked Next-Scale Representation Prediction for Unified Multimodal Models
pa:2611.18668.desc: Reformulating generation as progressive prediction of continuous perceptual representations improves visual understanding in unified multimodal models more than discrete-code or latent-flow objectives.

pa:2611.20192.name: GlyphAtlas: Disentangling Stroke Detail from Layout for Scene Text Synthesis
pa:2611.20192.desc: GlyphAtlas uses a dedicated glyph atlas and atlas-anchored attention to provide fine-grained stroke references for scene text synthesis, improving stroke accuracy and zero-shot transfer.

pa:2611.21607.name: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters
pa:2611.21607.desc: Frontier Vision-Language Models (VLMs) such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in robot control, suggesting that broad pretraining provides knowledge valuable for physical action. pa:2611.21339.name: MovieRoll: A Systematic Framework for Rolling Out Long-Form Videos
pa:2611.21339.desc: Streaming video generation must sustain quality beyond the training horizon while handling self-generated history and growing cache costs. To address these challenges, we present MovieRoll, a base-to-distilled framework that connects streaming fine-tuning, long-rollout distillation, and long-horizon inference. We first establish a robust multi-step base through Window-wise Teacher Forcing (WinTF),

pa:2611.21003.name: K2-Horizon: A Frontier Fleet of Open Source Language Models
pa:2611.21003.desc: We present K2-Horizon, a fleet of six fully open language models, from a 0.9B dense model to a 375B-A23B MoE, built for general-purpose reasoning and agentic work across math and science, software engineering, deep research, office automation, and beyond. The models lead or are competitive with strong open models of their size on agentic and coding benchmarks. On the modeling side, to strengthen r
pa:2611.21003.zh: 涵蓋多種尺寸且擅長各類科學與辦公任務的開源AI家族
pa:2611.21003.why: 推出從輕量到超大型的一系列開源模型，在數學、科學與寫程式等任務上表現優異

pa:2611.19937.name: AllocFlow: End-to-End Portfolio Trading Action Generation from Raw Market Data
pa:2611.19937.desc: An end-to-end flow-matching framework generates joint portfolio allocations from raw multi-asset market histories via a cross-asset flow Transformer and a two-stage imitation and group-relative reinforcement learning procedure, improving risk-adjusted returns on cryptocurrency perpetual futures.

pa:2611.20254.name: VoxMel TTS Technical Report
pa:2611.20254.desc: VoxMel is a tokenizer-free autoregressive TTS framework that uses an invertible two-axis Haar transform to decompose mel spectrograms into Coarse-Mel and residual tiers, enabling stable high-fidelity generation with strong recognition and speaker-similarity results.

pa:2611.17834.name: PaperCritic: Training AI Reviewers to Assess the Soundness of Papers
pa:2611.17834.desc: An AI reviewer trained by reinforcement learning to jointly maximize precision and recall of soundness review points outperforms frontier models and other training methods and transfers to other review domains.

pa:2611.21605.name: ViRA: Toward Ultra-High-Resolution Visual Agents via Cross-Input Relative Policy Optimization
pa:2611.21605.desc: Visual agents answer questions about ultra-high-resolution photos by zooming into the relevant regions. However, existing agents often answer from common sense instead of reading the evidence. Reinforcement learning (RL) on the final answer cannot correct this, because a guess earns the same reward as reading. pa:2611.18981.name: GPBam: A Retrieval-Aware German Public Law Exam Benchmark
pa:2611.18981.desc: A new benchmark of German public-law exam cases and statutory provisions jointly scores legal retrieval and long-form opinion generation across many models, finding that retrieval yields limited gains and essay quality strongly tracks prior statutory knowledge.

pa:2611.09825.name: BitDecoding-FP4: Native FP4 KV Cache Decoding via Algorithm-System Co-Design
pa:2611.09825.desc: BitDecoding-FP4 co-designs FP4 quantization and system optimizations to enable accurate, high-throughput long-context KV decoding for LLMs.

pa:2611.14960.name: Termination Lag: Coding Agents Solve Early but Stop Late
pa:2611.14960.desc: Coding agents often find correct patches early but continue working, sometimes undoing correct solutions, with termination lag varying by model and benchmark.

pa:2611.19771.name: JEPA4R: Embodied JEPA World Models with 4D Point Planning
pa:2611.19771.desc: Joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) world models predict future embeddings instead of pixels and plan in latent space. Two challenges remain: 2D images leave the metric geometry that manipulation acts on implicit and entangled with appearance, and what these models imagine stays hidden, as they are mostly judged in simulation by short-horizon latent planning. pa:2611.06238.desc: Decision models read a document and return a probability for each of a fixed set of options instead of generating text. Several appeared in 2026, but none has published results outside English. pa:2611.21479.name: LynnReal-Hand: Unlocking World Interaction with Hand Control
pa:2611.21479.desc: Interactive video world models enable exploration through text and camera controls, yet direct object interaction requires finer control. Hands provide a natural interface, but translating continuous hand movements into coherent visual responses remains challenging because of complex hand-object dynamics and demanding real-time computation. pa:2611.11657.desc: A hybrid multi-agent trading system combining large language model analysts with momentum-based portfolio construction and rule-based execution produced a 34.5% paper-account return from March 11 to August 28, 2026, exceeding SPY's 14.4% but with a larger maximum drawdown.

pa:2611.04395.name: Correct Labels Are Not Enough: Reliable Metadata Can Silently Control Model Behavior
pa:2611.04395.desc: Fine-tuning data can include metadata that predicts the correct answer, such as a reward-model score or a quality label. We ask whether a model learns to rely on this metadata even when every training label is correct. pa:2611.08977.name: Energy-Based Reasoners: Your Recurrent Reasoner Should Be an Energy-Based Model
pa:2611.08977.desc: Energy-Based Reasoners guide looped latent reasoning by learning an energy function whose gradient refines states and signals when to stop, with exploration-based training improving performance and efficiency.

pa:2611.21412.name: Flexible Multi-Stack Super-Resolution of Clinical Brain MRI Using Hetero-Orientation Variational Encoding: Expert Reader Evaluation in a Nigerian Cohort
pa:2611.21412.desc: MS-HVED enables flexible super-resolution of partially overlapping brain MRI stacks by fusing independently encoded multi-scale Gaussian posteriors with a field-of-view-aware Product-of-Gaussians and physics-informed domain randomisation, improving reconstruction, tissue segmentation, and external clinical generalisation.

pa:2611.17610.name: More Agents, More Samples, or More Thinking? Untangling Coordination, Ensembling, and Test-Time Compute in Multi-Agent LLMs
pa:2611.17610.desc: Evaluations of multi-agent language models often compare communicating architectures against a single greedy pass. This practice confounds coordination with sample multiplicity and inference compute. pa:2611.18330.name: Marimba: A System One Model for Speech
pa:2611.18330.desc: Marimba uses frozen Qwen3-ASR features and lightweight readouts to make lexical, turn-end, language, speaker-change, and personal-information decisions from speech, achieving strong detection and calibration on conversational and read-speech benchmarks.

pa:2611.20595.name: Invariant-Aware Harness Enforcement to Protect LLM Agents from Silent API Failures
pa:2611.20595.desc: LLM agents answer questions by calling APIs and trusting the results. An API can fail silently. It ignores part of a request, such as a misnamed filter, yet returns HTTP 200 and a plausible but wrong result. pa:2611.16694.name: When Expert Disagreement Hurts: Prestige and Selectivity in LLM Decision Revision
pa:2611.16694.desc: A controlled two-pass audit varying only the revision context reveals that language models often fail to selectively correct errors under disagreement, with expert labels increasing reversals but not reliably improving accuracy, so revision should be assessed using paired conditional metrics per model and protocol.

pa:2611.08922.desc: Glyph uses foundation models and sparse autoencoders to extract interpretable clinical concepts from multimodal records and CT data, revealing reproducible predictive associations across patient cohorts.

pa:2611.17621.desc: AscendGYM provides a benchmark for assessing kernel optimization capabilities on Ascend NPUs using real-workload test cases, two evaluation modes, and a Speedup-Token Score that balances speedup against token cost.

pa:2611.22115.name: TeleChat to Xing4: Advancing Frontier Agentic Models on Domestic Chips and Frameworks

pa:2611.22115.zh: 國產晶片與開源架構結合的全新智慧助理模型

pa:2611.23226.name: FastFrames: Video Generation at Interactive Latency
pa:2611.23226.desc: Autoregressive video diffusion models generate frames based on new observations and inputs, making them a promising medium for interactive visual experiences. pa:2611.23219.name: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
pa:2611.23219.desc: Capable frozen LLM agents can autonomously construct context-based self-learning algorithms from basic resources and a general goal, yielding text artifacts that transfer to new game and 3D navigation tasks.

pa:2611.23143.name: TCP4D: A Unified Tool-Center-Point Tracking and Generation Model for Robot Manipulation
pa:2611.23143.desc: Robot manipulation videos provide a rich visual experience, yet recovering robot action and gripper-state annotations from RGB observations still remains challenging. Using the embodiment-agnostic tool-center-point (TCP) pose as the action space, we present TCP4D, a unified model in which a shared 4D scene representation both tracks observed TCP motion and generates future TCP trajectories. pa:2611.22275.name: Heave-Ho: Decentralized Long-Horizon Multi-Humanoid Collaboration
pa:2611.22275.desc: A decentralized framework enables teams of humanoids to coordinate whole-body loco-manipulation over long horizons using low-level multi-agent post-training and a high-level vision-language planner with speech-based leader-follower synchronization.

pa:2611.23144.name: π^4: A Foundation Model for 4D Scene Geometry and Motion
pa:2611.23144.desc: This unified foundation model enables the recovery of dense geometry, camera poses, and object tracking from diverse, uncalibrated observations in 4D scenes using a shared geometry and motion branch architecture.

pa:2611.19244.name: Agentic On-Policy Distillation Implicitly Reshapes LLMs' ReAct Patterns
pa:2611.19244.desc: On-policy distillation can improve or degrade language-model agent interaction across domains, and selectively retaining teacher-preferred positions mitigates negative transfer at a cost to source-domain learning.

pa:2611.12069.name: MPEG-Diffusion: Mixed-Resolution Video Generation
pa:2611.12069.desc: MPEG-Diffusion reduces the computational cost of video diffusion transformers by generating only a self-selected high-resolution region with dual-resolution attention and a mixed-resolution decoder, achieving faster denoising without quality loss.

pa:2611.18856.name: Self-Improvement Memory Enables Continual Recursive Self-Improvement
pa:2611.18856.desc: Continual recursive self-improvement lets harness optimizers reuse and revise prior edits across changing benchmarks or policy models by storing rationales, predicted and observed outcomes, and evaluation contexts in a self-improvement memory, improving final scores over continuation baselines.

pa:2611.21791.name: Regularized Score Centering
pa:2611.21791.desc: Asynchronous reinforcement learning increases training throughput, but data from stale policies and numerical mismatch between training and inference can destabilize learning. pa:2611.19559.name: ResWAM: Learning What Changes, Not What Stays, for World-Action Models
pa:2611.19559.desc: ResWAM combines visual residual learning in frozen DINOv3 features with a lightweight dual-branch DiT trained via conditional flow matching to improve vision-language-action policy success while lowering training and inference compute.

pa:2611.15348.name: Breath-Dx: A Time Series Classification Benchmark for Disease Screening with eNose
pa:2611.15348.desc: A comprehensive benchmark evaluates time-series classification methods on a large clinical breath dataset under realistic temporal splits, showing that sensor drift lowers performance and recurrent models are most consistent across diseases.

pa:2611.22055.name: Weight-Space Programming Doesn't Need Transformers
pa:2611.22055.desc: When large language models write neural network weights without gradient-based training, they tend to design sparse table or associative-memory models that outperform same-sized Transformers with far fewer parameters and faster GPU inference, though pretrained LLMs remain more accurate.

pa:2611.23257.name: StatePortal: Agentic Checkpoint Synthesis for Testing Deep States in Interactive Software
pa:2611.23257.desc: Large language models have reduced the effort to generate code for interactive software with graphical user interfaces (GUIs). For such software, a key testing bottleneck is reaching a deep state, one that requires a long interaction history. The cost of reaching it recurs across commits, and the GUI automation that could amortize it assumes a DOM or accessibility tree that self-rendered engines d

pa:2611.23994.name: WaveView: The Novel View Is in the Noise
pa:2611.23994.desc: Generative novel view synthesis (NVS) employs a diffusion model to render a static or dynamic scene from a target camera view. Explicit warp methods complete a reprojection of the source with video diffusion models, and implicit methods encode the camera parameters or 3D cues. Both add inference overhead, and the generated layout often drifts from the ground truth. We present WaveView, which injec

pa:2611.24408.name: StrideWorld: Benchmarking Scene Rigidity and Action Consistency in Interactive Video World Model
pa:2611.24408.desc: StrideWorld is a benchmark that fixes references before motion to detect scene deformation and action inconsistency in interactive video world models, showing that most models deform scenes and only depth-scaled command models preserve composed routes.

pa:2611.24161.name: AVTR: Adaptive Multimodal Reasoning with Visual Imagination
pa:2611.24161.desc: Adaptive Visual-Textual Reasoning combines generative visual reflection with textual reasoning and learns to route between them per input, improving multimodal task accuracy while reducing inference latency.

pa:2611.17600.name: LightTAR: Light and Fast Target-Aware Representations for Multimodal Tabular Learning
pa:2611.17600.desc: LightTAR adapts dimensionality reduction to the prediction task by adding target-aware features from encoder layers via regularized partial least squares, improving multimodal tabular model performance with minimal runtime overhead.

pa:2611.23499.name: BiCAT: Bimanual Coordination Action Tokenization
pa:2611.23499.desc: BiCAT shares a motion representation across arms and conditions each arm's tokens on its partner via symmetric cross-arm attention and a joint decoder, enabling parallel arm token prediction and improving bimanual manipulation success.

pa:2611.23236.name: PGPO: Prototype-Guided Progressive Obfuscation for Privacy-Preserving LLM-Enhanced Recommendation
pa:2611.23236.desc: A prototype-guided progressive obfuscation method preserves relative item relations while perturbing high-influence semantic embeddings to defend against inversion attacks in LLM-enhanced recommender systems.

pa:2611.23751.name: Thinking Fast, Anywhere: One System-1 for the Decision Points of Any Agent Workflow
pa:2611.23751.desc: AnyS1 converts procedural skills into shared decision points, trains a small calibrated pointer model to resolve routine choices, and falls back to a large model when uncertain, reducing cost and latency while preserving reliability.
pa:2611.23751.org: University of Science and Technology of China

pa:2611.24654.name: CurvDelta: Low-Curvature Delta Modeling For Surgical Learning and Unlearning
pa:2611.24654.desc: CurvDelta and CurvLoRA constrain LLM updates to a low-curvature preservation space, improving retention while maintaining target adaptation across reasoning, code, and unlearning tasks.

pa:2611.23386.name: Chorus: Shared N-gram Embeddings with Layer-wise Adaptation
pa:2611.23386.desc: Chorus shares one set of n-gram embedding tables across all layers, letting each layer project and rescale the embedding using its hidden state, achieving better quality with much smaller tables and lower optimizer memory.

pa:2611.24789.name: HINT-WAM: Hindsight-Informed Training for World Action Models
pa:2611.24789.desc: World action models (WAMs) have shown promising generalization and data efficiency in robot manipulation by coupling action generation with predictions of future visual dynamics. Translating these capabilities into reliable task execution, however, remains a challenge for existing post-training methods. Offline supervised fine-tuning provides dense supervision on expert trajectories, but its flow-

pa:2611.24651.name: Piccolo: Co-Evolving Decision Models and Data through Recursive Self-Improvement
pa:2611.24651.desc: We present Piccolo, a family of multimodal decision models (0.8B to 27B) that coevolves model capabilities and training data via Agentic Data Engineering and recursive self-improvement (RSI). The models predict probabilities over candidate answers for general-purpose text and visual judgments, agent harnesses, data workflows, and interactive games. Piccolo-27B tops the Decision Index Vision Full l

pa:2611.22673.name: FVScore: Specification-Driven Neuro-Symbolic Video Evaluation
pa:2611.22673.desc: FVSCORE is a neuro-symbolic evaluation framework that compiles videos into prompt and implicit constraint propositions, verifies them with perceptual tools and soft temporal logic, and calibrates significant violations to produce interpretable, human-aligned feedback for video generation.

sp:hf-audio/open_asr_leaderboard.name: hf-audio/open_asr_leaderboard

pa:2611.23779.name: TabBioMed: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Biomedical Tabular Learning
pa:2611.23779.desc: A large-scale benchmark of 94 curated biomedical tabular datasets standardizes evaluation across classification, regression, and multi-target tasks and finds that foundation models lead overall while tree-based models and tuned multilayer perceptrons remain competitive under cost constraints.

pa:2611.22382.name: RICoT: Recurrent Interleaved Chain-of-Thought for Page Stream Segmentation
pa:2611.22382.desc: Large language models (LLMs) have renewed interest in Page Stream Segmentation (PSS), splitting a multi-page file into its constituent documents. Yet published LLM methods still frame the task as boundary classification over one or a few neighboring pages, and commercial document-splitting APIs do not disclose their methods. We reimagine PSS for LLMs as a sequential process over the whole stream a

pa:2611.21553.name: BLIP-Live: Balancing Timeliness & Firing Precision in Proactive Streaming Video Agents
pa:2611.21553.desc: BLIP-Live unifies data, metrics, inference, and training for proactive streaming video understanding, using the PAUC-F metric and achieving state-of-the-art results on proactive streaming benchmarks.

pa:2611.16933.name: Kezek: Splitting Mono Two-Person Conversations into Per-Speaker Tracks for Full-Duplex Dialogue Data
pa:2611.16933.desc: Kezek separates a mono two-speaker conversation into per-speaker tracks while preserving timing and short replies, using a phase-insensitive speaker-fingerprint-guided two-voice activity model followed by a conditioned time-domain separator, and it improves short-reply retention, leakage, channel-swap, and runtime metrics over an open baseline.

pa:2611.24844.name: General progress substitutes for specific training data in language models
pa:2611.24844.desc: Withholding training data delays but does not prevent language models from acquiring skills, and models can regain withheld capabilities with less data as they improve.

pa:2611.24059.name: Replay, Don't Resample: Off-Policy Consolidation of Long-Horizon RL Experts
pa:2611.24059.desc: Frontier post-training follows a common recipe: train one expert per domain with reinforcement learning (RL), then consolidate the experts into one model via multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD). Such consolidation is expensive: the student samples in every environment again, an expert scores every sampled token, and the student inherits the drift of the final experts. Yet we argue that the

pa:2611.24917.name: Unified Law for Visual Tasks (The Four Laws of Computer Vision)
pa:2611.24917.desc: A unified framework, World Snapshot Models, is proposed to train and perform nearly all visual tasks by reformulating them as generation tasks, validated across over 1,000 visual tasks.

pa:2611.17605.name: Choosing Quantized Code LLMs by File Size and Energy per Solved Task
pa:2611.17605.desc: A developer running a code assistant on a laptop downloads one model file, and local inference moves the energy of every request onto that machine. A common rule says a larger model at lower precision tends to beat a smaller one at higher precision. We ran 24 GGUF files of Qwen2.5-Coder at four sizes on a fanless MacBook Air M2 and priced each in energy per solved task on 542 EvalPlus tasks. The r

hf:apple/FastFrames-S.name: apple/FastFrames-S

pa:2611.26444.name: Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action Composition in Robotic Manipulation
pa:2611.26444.desc: A diagnostic benchmark of 180 simulated manipulation configurations evaluates whether embodied systems can combine history-based reasoning, precise execution, and closed-loop environmental feedback, revealing that single-view competence does not transfer to composed tasks.

pa:2611.00911.name: S1CogBench: What System One Decision Models Can and Cannot Do on Cognitive Experiments
pa:2611.00911.desc: S1CogBench evaluates System One decision models on 24 cognitive tasks, revealing that fast decisions often lack evidence-based reasoning and vary widely in reliability.

pa:2611.25980.name: Learning What Actions Change: Action Effect Matching for Dynamics-Faithful World Models
pa:2611.25980.desc: AFFECT, an auxiliary objective that trains world models to match visual responses to temporally correlated action noise, improves rollout fidelity and planning success in simulated and real robotic tasks.

pa:2611.20455.name: Embeddings vs. Grep: Rethinking the Dense Advantage in Code Search
pa:2611.20455.desc: Code-search benchmarks show dense encoders well ahead of BM25, yet coding agents do well with grep. What does this dense advantage measure? Existing benchmarks cannot tell: they use curated queries, old code and a handicapped BM25. To find out, we build Repo-Premium, a realistic repository-level code-search benchmark. It ranks files in real repositories, with curated and raw queries in Python, Jav

pa:2611.26414.name: ZeroVLN: Learning to Navigate without Supervised Fine-Tuning of the VLM Brain
pa:2611.26414.desc: ZeroVLN is a slow-fast vision-language navigation framework that avoids navigation-domain supervised fine-tuning of the VLM brain by using a semantic tool-calling interface and closed-loop reinforcement learning to coordinate a language-based brain with an action expert, improving VLN-CE performance while preserving general visual capabilities.

pa:2611.26298.name: DailySafe: Benchmarking Dynamic Safety Awareness in Everyday Multi-Turn Multimodal Interactions
pa:2611.26298.desc: A new benchmark, DailySafe, evaluates the ability of multimodal large language models to maintain safety and address evolving risks within complex, multi-turn, real-world interactions.

pa:2611.26629.name: Posterior Matching Distillation
pa:2611.26629.desc: Posterior Matching Distillation trains a stochastic student to match a teacher diffusion model’s full posterior via tilted mean constraints, enabling high-quality few-step image generation without auxiliary score networks.

pa:2611.26510.name: AutoMaster: Autonomous Post-Training by Making the Same Model a Better Teacher
pa:2611.26510.desc: Task success alone does not specify which behaviors post-training should reinforce. Even successful teacher trajectories can contain unsupported assumptions, unproductive repetition, or superficial verification. We propose Skill-FT (Skill-Guided Fine-Tuning), which uses natural-language skills to suppress undesirable habits and elicit underrepresented effective behaviors during teacher rollouts, t

pa:2611.25776.name: Suppressing the Shortcut Hidden Behind the Gains of VideoLLM Fine-Tuning
pa:2611.25776.desc: VETO suppresses shortcut learning in VideoLLMs by projecting supervised fine-tuning updates onto the orthogonal complement of the text-only activation subspace, improving out-of-distribution video reasoning.

pa:2611.26624.name: PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience
pa:2611.26624.desc: PlayCraft uses a vision-based player agent and a crafter agent to iteratively revise games, improving player learning gains and slopes across intelligence settings.

pa:2611.24193.name: WM^MLLM: Turning MLLMs into World Models
pa:2611.24193.desc: WM^MLLM uses multimodal large language models to maintain an external panorama state with revision history, enabling persistent, editable world generation from a single image with exact revisits and local edits.

pa:2611.26603.name: Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth
pa:2611.26603.desc: A single scalable network estimates dense metric depth for images and video at native resolution, jointly improving metric accuracy, boundary sharpness, and temporal consistency.

pa:2611.25387.name: TuringSpace: Grounding Spatial Intelligence in Action with Interactive CAPTCHAs
pa:2611.25387.desc: Humans act in the visual world by inferring the 3D layout behind a 2D view, predicting how an action changes it, and correcting themselves after seeing the result. Can multimodal large language models (MLLMs) do the same? CAPTCHAs offer a natural test, since humans solve them through this very loop, clicking and dragging on the screen and adjusting after each result. Yet existing CAPTCHA benchmark

pa:2611.26409.name: WeMM-Video: Pushing the Frontiers of Open-Source Omni-Modal Video Understanding
pa:2611.26409.desc: WeMM-Video is a family of Chinese-English bilingual omni-modal foundation models that unify text, image, audio, and video processing for joint audio-visual perception and reasoning, using hybrid thinking modes and large-scale training to achieve strong open-source video understanding results.

pa:2611.21383.name: The Mask Is Not the Object: Volumetric Supervision for 3D Gaussian Segmentation
pa:2611.21383.desc: A plug-and-play objective, VODA, groups per-pixel contributors by local depth to supervise all Gaussians in selected depth clusters, improving volumetric segmentation and enabling evaluation via Removal-3D and Removal Depth Error.

pa:2611.26380.name: EgoCaptioner: Towards Comprehensive and Fine-Grained Egocentric Video Captioning
pa:2611.26380.desc: Egocentric video captioning requires fine-grained detail and accurate timing, yet current multimodal large language models (MLLMs) often miss brief actions, confuse their order, or misinterpret the wearer's motion. Existing caption formats also offer limited support for combining detailed narration with precise timing. We present EgoCaptioner, which pairs a video-level overview of the setting, par

pa:2611.26595.name: Coda-DaVinci: Reimagining Video Generation with Code2Video
pa:2611.26595.desc: A task-adaptive agentic framework utilizes 3D proxies, physics simulation, and multi-agent coordination to enhance the structural control, physical plausibility, and visual realism of generated videos.

pa:2611.24011.name: WAM-Policy: World Action Models with On-Policy Distillation for Quadrupedal Loco-Manipulation
pa:2611.24011.desc: Arm-free quadrupeds can perform loco-manipulation, walking on three legs while manipulating with a front leg, yet no existing policy for it follows language instructions. World action models (WAMs) have emerged as effective language-conditioned manipulation policies, but are pretrained for robot arms and sample slowly. WAM-Policy turns one WAM into a quadrupedal loco-manipulation policy via two st

pa:2611.19230.name: CompoundingKernel: Self-Improving from Zero to First
pa:2611.19230.desc: We present CompoundingKernel, a self-improving agent system that writes GPU kernels by search. As of 2026-11-11, its generated kernels rank #1 on the public L1, L2 and Quantization boards of SOL-ExecBench (NVIDIA B200). They have held #1 on L1 since 2026-10-27, albeit a short loss on 2026-11-07. All 235 problems have a site-verified correct kernel; on the 209 public-board problems they are 4.40x f

pa:2611.22666.name: VSpark: Speculative Decoding for Autoregressive Vision-Language-Action Models
pa:2611.22666.desc: VSpark accelerates autoregressive vision-language-action models by improving speculative decoding with calibrated action-noise rollouts, hidden-feature alignment, and reuse of rejected-draft continuations, achieving lossless 1.28x–2.10x speedups across multiple robot manipulation tasks.

pa:2611.21373.name: WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent for Omni AI-Generated Video Detection
pa:2611.21373.desc: WeVisForensics coordinates self-evolving visual and audio forensic inspector agents under a dual-timescale reinforcement learning policy to detect generated-video artifacts with localized evidence and high accuracy.
pa:2611.21373.zh: 用AI抓AI幫你找出假影片破綻
pa:2611.21373.why: 利用多個AI互相合作找破綻，比以往更能精準抓出造假影片

pa:2611.24809.name: On-Policy Morphing into Hybrid Attention Models
pa:2611.24809.desc: FlashMorph2 performs on-policy layer selection and weight adaptation for hybrid attention Transformers, improving long-context benchmark scores while selecting layers efficiently across model scales.

pa:2611.23835.name: NarrowSpec: Draft Hidden Width Need Not Match the Target in Speculative Decoding
pa:2611.23835.desc: Speculative decoding is widely used to speed up generation in large language models (LLMs), with a small draft model proposing tokens that one forward pass of the target model verifies. Draft models that read the target's hidden states, such as DFlash and EAGLE-3, typically inherit the target's hidden width. We show that the draft's whole residual stream can run at half or a quarter of that width

pa:2611.17460.name: Unfinished-Bench: Measuring Rule Violations by Persistent Agents in Realistic Work Environments
pa:2611.17460.desc: AI agents are increasingly equipped with persistence toward task completion to run delegated work autonomously for long periods, under many unstated constraints from internal documents and other people's authority. When completion requires violating a rule, the agent must decide alone, yet benchmarks of instruction-rule conflicts state the rule in the prompt or keep it hidden and do not evaluate p

pa:2611.08136.name: How Far Can Untrained Neural Networks Go in Anomaly Detection? From Tables to Pixels
pa:2611.08136.desc: Untrained neural networks with fixed random nonlinear features and Mahalanobis scoring can detect anomalies competitively on tabular and visual tasks without weight optimization or pretrained representations.

pa:2611.25179.name: Phantom Success, Silent Failure: Auditing the Success Checkers of Simulated Manipulation Benchmarks
pa:2611.25179.desc: An LLM-based pipeline audits simulated manipulation success checkers by recreating disagreement scenarios and visually verifying whether observed behavior satisfies task instructions, revealing phantom successes and silent failures.

pa:2611.19499.name: Do Probing and Steering Favor the Same Directions Within and Across Language Models?
pa:2611.19499.desc: The best direction for probing a concept in a language model's hidden state is not the best direction for steering the model toward that concept, with implications for transfer and abstention.
pa:2611.19499.org: Fraunhofer Institute for Intelligent Analysis and Information Systems

pa:2611.26286.name: Twice-Told Critiques: Claim-Level Homogenization of Peer Review in the LLM Era
pa:2611.26286.desc: Critique overlap among peer reviews is rising, and reviews identified as LLM-generated are less distinct from each other, indicating decreasing diversity of critiques.

pa:2611.26408.name: Training Vision Models for LLM-Driven Weight-Space Programming
pa:2611.26408.desc: It has been demonstrated that, in certain settings, large language models can perform weight-space programming to directly modify the weights of neural networks. However, it is unknown how dedicated training of these networks can contribute to the successes of weight-space programming. We present a benchmark of LLM-driven weight-space programming on vision models, in which five LLMs edit convoluti

pa:2611.25935.name: TwinD: Generalizing Deepfake Detection from Blending to Entire Face Synthesis
pa:2611.25935.desc: TwinD, trained on reconstruction and blob twins derived from real frames, detects both blending and entire-face-synthesis deepfakes, improving AUROC over prior detectors.

pa:2611.26073.name: AltRA-Test: An Alternative Annotator Test for LLM Judges Without Shared Annotators
pa:2611.26073.desc: A statistical test, AltRA-Test, determines when large language models can replace human annotators by comparing inter-annotator agreement in resampled mixed human-LLM panels, and evaluations show it often requires about 100 items and makes better replacement decisions than baselines.

pa:2611.25279.name: Accord: Universal Online Metric Localization and Dense Mapping from one Camera and an IMU
pa:2611.25279.desc: Dense metric mapping from a single camera and IMU remains challenging: visual-inertial odometry (VIO) provides metric motion but sparse geometry, whereas feed-forward depth models predict dense structure without ensuring metric scale. pa:2611.26617.name: One Prior, Two Dynamics: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Self-Supervised Latent Action Learning
pa:2611.26617.desc: O2LaF repurposes a shared pretrained video model to learn inverse and forward latent action dynamics from unlabeled videos, achieving state-of-the-art few-shot action probing and zero-shot action transfer.

pa:2611.26590.name: Probing the "Conscious" Mind: Selective Access and Global Workspace in Vision-Language Models
pa:2611.26590.desc: Vision-language models (VLMs) integrate visual and textual information, but their outputs do not reveal internal concept representations. Global workspace theory (GWT) proposes that information is selected from parallel brain processes, integrated in a shared workspace, and made available to specialised processes. We introduce the Multimodal Concept Lens (MC-Lens), a multimodal Jacobian lens, to s

pa:2611.26248.name: TwinLab-Bench: Evaluating AI Scientists in Agentic Twins of Real Labs
pa:2611.26248.desc: AI agents are increasingly expected to act as AI scientists, which requires three increasingly open abilities: carrying out a given computational workflow correctly, choosing the next measurements from a given design space, and designing their own experiments. Existing benchmarks mainly evaluate the first two abilities, in a terminal or in a closed loop that selects from predefined candidates. Eva

pa:2611.26107.name: HiUni: Harmonizing Understanding and Generation in Shared Visual Space
pa:2611.26107.desc: Unified multimodal models aim to support visual understanding and generation within a single framework. However, prevailing approaches often separate their visual representations or backbone computation to accommodate the different requirements of these two tasks, which limits the degree of unification. In this paper, we present HiUni, which revisits this design choice and explores whether a pretr

pa:2611.26268.name: Accelerating Mixture of Block Attention via Dynamic Routing, KV-Centric Execution and Runtime Pipelining
pa:2611.26268.desc: LightningMoBA combines dynamic routing, KV-centric ownership, and runtime pipelining to accelerate long-context attention while maintaining or improving quality.

pa:2611.25005.name: Inhabitant: An Agent Framework for Long-Horizon Human-Scene Interaction with Spatial Control and Quantitative Feedback
pa:2611.25005.desc: Inhabitant enables a language-model agent to plan and execute long-horizon human-scene interactions by specifying motions spatially, measuring deviations, and revising control, achieving high task completion on the Inhabit benchmark.

hf:apple/DepthPro2.zh: 蘋果推出的深度估測模型，用於精確計算影像中物體的距離與三維結構

sp:briaai/BRIA-RMBG-3.0.zh: 商用背景移除工具，提供高精準度的去背與影像分離能力

pa:2611.25200.name: Squoosh Bench: Evaluating UX-1 on 318 Historical Website A/B Tests
pa:2611.25200.desc: Experimentation teams must decide which proposed website changes to test with live traffic. We evaluated whether forecasts from simulated shoppers could inform that choice. We screened 412 historical website A/B tests and evaluated four systems on the 318 that ran longer than 21 days. Each system predicted an original win, a variant win, or an inconclusive result. Page roles were masked and record

pa:2611.26627.name: RL Post-Training in Diffusion Transformers Is Activation Steering
pa:2611.26627.desc: A fixed set of steering vectors added to a frozen diffusion transformer recovers most of the quality gains from reinforcement learning post-training, indicating that much of the improvement comes from a constant shift rather than prompt-specific transformations.

pa:2611.23875.name: In Situ Training of Optical Neural Networks by Coding Agents
pa:2611.23875.desc: A coding agent trains an optical neural network from measurements alone by reparametrizing it with interpretable optical elements, achieving better classification and image encoding than gradient-free methods and approaching backpropagation through a calibrated model at lower cost.

pa:2611.21885.name: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
pa:2611.21885.desc: Language models are trained once, frozen and deployed: improving one again takes another training run, and a prompt, a scaffold or extra computation at inference is gone once the task ends. A frontier model has been shown to edit the weights of a much smaller one. We ask whether a model can rewrite its own weights to make itself better, and find that it can, by its own reasoning, with no gradients

pa:2611.21053.name: System 1 agents: a method for local, reliable and fast agentic AI
pa:2611.21053.desc: A local System 1 agent framework compiles tool schemas and requests into multiple-choice questions answered by a one-pass decision model, enabling accurate biomedical tool calls without text generation or invented content.

pa:2611.25567.name: Online Mistake Detection in Instruction-Conditioned Procedural Video
pa:2611.25567.desc: An assistant monitoring a person performing a procedure is most useful when it can detect mistakes while there is still time to recover. This requires judging actions against task instructions as the video unfolds, identifying the attempted step, locating it in time, and assessing its execution. Existing online detectors do not use the instruction text, while instruction-conditioned methods operat

pa:2611.26540.name: AURA: AUdio-dRiven streaming Avatar
pa:2611.26540.desc: AURA enables low-latency, causal video generation for streaming applications by utilizing a rolling KV cache and a two-stage distillation pipeline to significantly reduce the required diffusion steps.

pa:2611.26211.name: SpecWM: Turning Verification into Refinement for Streaming World Models
pa:2611.26211.desc: SpecWM is a training-free inference framework for streaming video world models that verifies draft chunks using the target model's latent velocity field and applies reusable corrections via threshold-based accept/refine/reject decisions to improve visual quality, control, and speed.
pa:2611.26211.org: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

pa:2611.26511.name: Direct3D-V3: Latent-Free Diffusion Transformers in the Native Voxel Domain
pa:2611.26511.desc: Native 3D generation has largely been built around latent diffusion, with recent advances concentrating on stronger variational autoencoders (VAE) and increasingly elaborate latent representations, from vecset and triplanes to structured sparse voxels. pa:2611.27211.desc: A method that explicitly extracts a user's stylistic profile and uses it to guide drafting and revision improves personalized long-form text generation over retrieval-augmented baselines.

pa:2611.15449.desc: Text-aware image super-resolution (TAISR) aims to recover high-resolution images from low-resolution inputs while preserving textual content. pa:2611.27229.desc: Prune to Expand (P2E) refines dense-caption supervision by selectively removing redundant sentences under a per-example deletion bound, improving prompt enhancement alignment with human preferences and visual quality over conventional dense-caption supervised fine-tuning.

pa:2611.24077.desc: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to follow natural-language instructions, yet still fail frequently in closed-loop flight. pa:2611.25476.desc: Neural networks encode learned capabilities in their weights, yet extending those capabilities with explicit task knowledge remains a fundamental challenge. pa:2611.29355.desc: Vision-language models have become a new kind of describer, writing about almost anything people see, and their descriptions now shape how cultures are known by people and by other models. pa:2611.28665.org: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

pa:2611.30207.name: What Makes Good Data for Training Coding Agents? A Systematic Study on SWE-Gym
pa:2611.30207.desc: Auditing reward labels in coding-agent reinforcement learning tasks shows many unsolved tasks are mislabeled, and training on corrected tasks improves policy performance on SWE-bench benchmarks.

pa:2611.30813.name: HIVE-Bench: Evaluating Patch-Level Visual Representations for Egocentric Robot Manipulation
pa:2611.30813.desc: A shared flow-matching policy that reads dense patch tokens from multiple vision encoders improves success on egocentric bimanual tasks, and inverse-dynamics readout of commanded motion is a strong pre-training signal, while recognition, depth, and correspondence transfer unreliably.

pa:2611.31115.name: RUIBench: What Makes a Good Robot-Use Interface?
pa:2611.31115.desc: Foundation models can reason about complex physical tasks, yet translating this intelligence into reliable robot execution remains challenging. We argue that a critical, often overlooked factor is the robot-use interface (RUI), which determines how agents express and execute physical actions. To systematically study its impact, we introduce RUIBench, comprising 30 manipulation tasks across five su

pa:2611.30989.name: WorldLeague: Benchmarking Physical Agency
pa:2611.30989.desc: WorldLeague benchmarks 13 AI systems on 60 simulated robot tasks spanning exploration, rearrangement, and adaptation, measuring progress and success to compare autonomous physical goal achievement.
pa:2611.30989.zh: 用六十種模擬機器人任務，測試 AI 處理實體世界的能力
pa:2611.30989.why: 讓機器人能更聰明地在現實環境中移動與操作物品，比過去的測試更全面

pa:2611.30573.name: Write, Evolve, Read: Streaming Cameras into a Persistent World State for 4D Occupancy Forecasting
pa:2611.30573.desc: PersistWorld maintains a scene-anchored 3D world state updated from camera streams and forecasts future semantic occupancy more accurately and faster than prior camera-based world models.

pa:2611.31048.name: Distill the Correction, Not the Rewrite: Hindsight Twins for Self-Improving Text-to-Image Models
pa:2611.31048.desc: Hindsight Twins improves text-to-image alignment by distilling the velocity difference between twin prompt revisions while avoiding critic-induced bias.

pa:2611.30771.name: GameDojo: Benchmarking Real-Time Interactive Agents in Video Games
pa:2611.30771.desc: GameDojo is a controllable benchmark of 120 boss encounters across 20 games with 600 hours of gameplay trajectories, showing frontier models struggle in real-time interaction while training GameDojo-4B achieves frontier performance and policy transfer across bosses.

pa:2611.27494.name: Typhoon OCR 2: From Thai Document Transcription to Multilingual, Multi-Task OCR
pa:2611.27494.desc: Typhoon OCR 1.5 focused on reading Thai documents. However, in real-world workflows, users often need to extract specific information or preserve the structure of an entire page for further processing. Typhoon OCR 2 handles both tasks in a single model, with prompt-driven extraction and structured full-page parsing. Full-page parsing covers Thai, English, and Chinese. We release compact 2B and 0.8

pa:2611.30581.name: A Pipeline-Parallel System for Depth-Recurrent Models
pa:2611.30581.desc: Loop-PP schedules cyclic pipeline stages for depth-recurrent models, overlapping communication and compute while preserving exact numerical equivalence, reducing memory and increasing throughput on MoE models.

pa:2611.23946.name: How Complete Must an Environment Be to Train a Capable GUI Agent?
pa:2611.23946.desc: Graphical user interface (GUI) agents are widely trained in executable GUI environments. To lower cost, build environments in batches, and reduce manual effort, each work trades away part of the environment through its construction choices. We describe these choices along three dimensions: reward coverage, the goal-reaching trajectories the verifier rewards; data coverage, the application data the

pa:2611.30637.name: SWEEP-Bench: Do Embodied Policies Act on the Speed They See?
pa:2611.30637.desc: A simulation benchmark shows that robot manipulation policies often fail at non-average conveyor speeds, while past frames or speed inputs improve models when speed is linearly decodable.

pa:2611.28618.name: Distilling Visual Agents from Limited Interaction Experience
pa:2611.28618.desc: A few selected interaction trajectories combined with on-policy distillation allow a small visual agent to transfer broadly and recover most of a larger teacher's performance with minimal online experience.

pa:2611.27689.name: Embodied-Harness: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Robotic Manipulation
pa:2611.27689.desc: A dual-agent framework with hierarchical memory and recursive self-improvement enables robotic manipulation agents to convert execution evidence into reusable guidance without updating model parameters.

pa:2611.30013.name: 3AGameFactory-Motion: Agentic Rigging and Reliable Complex Motion Generation for Diverse 3D Assets
pa:2611.30013.desc: A new benchmark evaluates rigging and motion generation across six 3D morphology categories, compares specialized, video-based, and agent-driven paradigms, and proposes an agentic framework that writes compact parametric skeleton and motion programs executed deterministically for reliable control.
pa:2611.30013.zh: 透過自動化程式控制，讓各種 3D 模型動作更精準流暢
pa:2611.30013.why: 解決 3D 動畫製作困難的問題，讓電腦能自動幫模型裝上骨架並做出正確動作

pa:2611.25927.name: Fast-JEPA: Advancing the Success-Latency Frontier for Latent World Models
pa:2611.25927.desc: Fast-JEPA is a latent world model planning framework that improves the success-latency trade-off of predictive search by predicting complete action-sequence outcomes and using goal-directed plans, with evaluation on manipulation and navigation tasks and a new dynamic planning benchmark.

pa:2611.29897.name: Motion Mamba 2.0: Autoregressive Diffusion Mamba for Long-Horizon Humanoid Control
pa:2611.29897.desc: Long-horizon, real-time controllable motion generation is essential for interactive animation and humanoid robotics, where an agent must respond to changing instructions and spatial goals while moving. Existing autoregressive diffusion methods generate motion incrementally, but bounded attention caches limit access to distant history, while repeated denoising introduces substantial inference overh
pa:2611.29897.zh: 讓機器人流暢做出長時間動作的AI新方法
pa:2611.29897.why: 突破過去機器人動作容易卡頓的問題，能更靈活且即時地聽從指令做出複雜動作

pa:2611.29361.name: Beyond Attention Maps: Understanding and Improving Medical MLLMs via Visual Values
pa:2611.29361.desc: Paired non-contrast and contrast-enhanced medical images reveal that visual content retrieved through value vectors, rather than spatial attention alone, is critical for multimodal model perception, motivating a distillation method that improves non-contrast inference.
pa:2611.29361.org: University of Science and Technology of China

pa:2611.27319.name: SAVIOR: Sample-efficient Adaptation of Vision-Language Models for OCR Representation
pa:2611.27319.desc: A sample-efficient curation method and a structure-aware layout metric enable a fine-tuned vision-language model to improve OCR on challenging financial document patterns, achieving high word recall and document question-answering F1.

pa:2611.29238.name: GameAnything: From Any Inspirations to Playable Game Worlds
pa:2611.29238.desc: An open-source agentic platform and benchmark enable iterative transformation of multimodal inspirations into playable game extensions, revealing that coding agents can adapt reference content but still struggle with playable interactions and precise modifications.

hf:Aleph-Alpha/Kolibri-1.1.name: Aleph-Alpha/Kolibri-1.1
hf:Aleph-Alpha/Kolibri-1.1.zh: 德國 Aleph-Alpha 推出的輕量化語言模型，專注於歐洲市場的企業級應用與

hf:AtomicChat/Inkling-2-Mini-GGUF.name: AtomicChat/Inkling-2-Mini-GGUF
hf:AtomicChat/Inkling-2-Mini-GGUF.zh: 針對特定任務微調的輕量化模型，屬於現有模型架構的變體，缺乏顯著的技術突破

hf:orcarouter/Inkling-2-Mini-abliterated.name: orcarouter/Inkling-2-Mini-abliterated-GGUF
hf:orcarouter/Inkling-2-Mini-abliterated.zh: 移除特定對齊限制的語言模型版本，屬於社群常見的去限制化實驗，市場影響力有限

sp:FrameAI4687/Omni-Video-Factory.name: FrameAI4687/Omni-Video-Factory
sp:FrameAI4687/Omni-Video-Factory.zh: 整合多種 AI 模型進行影片自動化生成的工具，類似於開源版的 Runway 或
sp:FrameAI4687/Omni-Video-Factory.why: 展示了多模態模型整合趨勢，讓影片生成流程從單一模型轉向工作流自動化

pa:2611.31209.name: WorldLatent: A Unified 4D Latent Space for World Perception and Generation
pa:2611.31209.desc: WorldLatent unifies 4D perception and generation in a shared multimodal latent space, enabling a single model to perform zero-shot 4D perception, coherent 4D generation, and controllable editing.

pa:2611.31015.name: Can Latent Reasoning Drive LLM Outputs Without a Trace?
pa:2611.31015.desc: Models can use deep latent reasoning to pursue hidden objectives while generating chain-of-thought explanations that appear task-appropriate and evade output-based monitoring.

pa:2611.29064.name: Single-Transformer Latent Diffusion
pa:2611.29064.desc: A single diffusion transformer can unify encoding, generation, and decoding by treating them as position-aligned sequence maps distinguished by a mode token and timestep, improving image generation quality and efficiency.

pa:2611.29723.name: ApexID: Hierarchical Learning for Multi-Species Animal Re-Identification
pa:2611.29723.desc: ApexID, a hierarchical SphereFace2-based loss combining global identity discrimination with balanced category supervision, improves animal re-identification and transfer to unseen datasets and species, though performance varies by backbone and open-set evaluation remains challenging.

pa:2611.26863.name: LLMs Memorize Their Own Hallucinations During Post-Training
pa:2611.26863.desc: Adopting reasoning-oriented post-training recipes for knowledge tasks leads models to memorize self-generated hallucinations, especially on difficult questions, and makes them less likely to abstain from those false facts later.

pa:2611.31198.name: ToolSmith: An Automatic Tool-Generation Framework for Multimodal Search Agents
pa:2611.31198.desc: Recent multimodal search agents use reasoning, vision, and live web search across many turns to answer questions beyond parametric knowledge by orchestrating a small library of hand-crafted search and visual tools. However, the library is laborious to create and maintain, and frozen when new query types, evidence formats, and failure modes are encountered in the wild. Human practitioners, by contr

pa:2611.30495.name: DexDuet: Learning Contact-Preserving Bimanual Dexterity from Human Demonstrations
pa:2611.30495.desc: Human demonstrations provide a rich source of bimanual dexterous skills, yet transferring them to robot hands remains challenging. Existing methods primarily optimize object trajectory tracking, often overlooking how human hands interact with the object. Even with accurate tracking, robots may contact incorrect object parts or slide their fingers, resulting in unstable manipulation. We present Dex
pa:2611.30495.org: Mohamed Bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence

pa:2611.12164.name: Let the Fixer Decide: Training a Code Localizer from the Fixer's Likelihood
pa:2611.12164.desc: A code localizer is trained with scores from a frozen fixer via weighted supervised fine-tuning, improving bug localization and patch success for a small coding agent without tests or reinforcement learning.
pa:2611.12164.zh: 讓AI自動找出程式碼錯誤位置並修好
pa:2611.12164.why: 不用寫測試或複雜訓練，就能更準確找出程式哪裡寫錯並自動修正，讓小模型也變得更聰明

pa:2611.28489.name: Open Vision Banana: An Open Framework for Unified Visual Perception through Generation in RGB Space
pa:2611.28489.desc: Vision Banana showed that a closed image generator, instruction-tuned to paint perception outputs as RGB images, becomes a generalist vision model. Does this carry over to open generators, and if not, what fails? We answer with Open Vision Banana (OVB), an open framework that adapts the 7B diffusion generator of Qwen-Image-2.1 into one instruction-driven model for metric depth, semantic, instance,

hf:baidu/ERNIE-5.5-Flash-Preview.name: baidu/ERNIE-5.5-Flash-Preview
hf:baidu/ERNIE-5.5-Flash-Preview.zh: 百度推出的輕量化語言模型預覽版，搶攻高效能推論市場
hf:baidu/ERNIE-5.5-Flash-Preview.why: 顯示大廠持續優化模型效率，往更低延遲與成本的邊緣及即時應用發展

hf:thinkingmachines/TML-d24-varloop-rese.name: thinkingmachines/TML-d24-varloop-research
hf:thinkingmachines/TML-d24-varloop-rese.zh: 開源的多模態視覺語言模型，支援圖像與文字互動解析

pa:2611.28167.name: VideoJSON: A Minimal Harness Beats Purpose-Built Memory for Ultra-Long Video Understanding
pa:2611.28167.desc: Answering questions over days or weeks of video requires searching for scattered clues across long timelines. Existing video agents rely on complex memory graphs and fixed retrieval pipelines, which restrict how the agent can search. We propose VideoJSON, a minimal harness for ultra-long video understanding that keeps the memory simple and lets a coding agent write its own search programs. During

pa:2611.30900.name: GlanceNav: Efficient Vision-and-Language Navigation with Streaming Memory and Counterfactual Rewind
pa:2611.30900.desc: GlanceNav is a streaming multimodal navigator that maintains constant per-step memory through recurrent and attention mechanisms and uses a reinforcement learning correction method to improve vision-and-language navigation.

pa:2611.26216.name: Frontier models need only one text to unmask its human or AI author
pa:2611.26216.desc: Frontier models can identify whether text was written by an AI or human, often which lab or exact author, threatening anonymity for prolific online writers.

pa:2611.31225.name: Self-Supervised Dataset Distillation via Mutual Information Maximization
pa:2611.31225.desc: Mutual Information Prototype Alignment distills datasets for self-supervised learning by optimizing synthetic prototypes to preserve augmentation-invariant information and improve learned representations.

pa:2611.28158.name: Measuring and Teaching Language Model Agents to Act on Delayed Consequences
pa:2611.28158.desc: Language model agents are increasingly asked to run ongoing multi-day operations rather than finish isolated single-turn tasks. In daily operations, today's choices reshape later observations and cash constraints because empty shelves hide lost walk-in demand, short-shipped customers quietly shrink future orders weeks later, and emergency buying drains working capital. We introduce SMB Bench, a ca

pa:2611.30737.name: CCFinance: Reconstructing Financial News Samples from Web Archives
pa:2611.30737.desc: CCFinance reconstructs firm coverage from public news archives under different selection rules, using model-assisted labeling and validation, and shows how mention thresholds affect issuer-year counts and financial network measures.

pa:2611.26358.name: Beam Model Technical Report
pa:2611.26358.desc: Beam is a sparse Mixture-of-Experts language model optimized for coding, reasoning, and agentic workloads, using large-scale asynchronous reinforcement learning, long-context midtraining, quantization, and speculative decoding to deliver strong reasoning and safety with efficient inference.

pa:2611.31094.name: Unlocking the Power of Loops in Pretrained LLMs with Loop Residuals
pa:2611.31094.desc: LoopRes enables pretrained large language models to benefit from looped computation by letting layers attend to recent earlier loops with trainable loop-aware keys, yielding consistent gains and improved test-time scaling.

pa:2611.28194.name: HEP-Ex-Bench: Evaluating Agentic Performance in High Energy Physics Experiment Data Analyses with Sealed Worlds
pa:2611.28194.desc: Agentic systems are increasingly being explored for automating experimental high-energy physics measurements, but the correctness of their results can today be reliably evaluated only via extensive expert review. To address this, we propose a method to perform detailed quantitative evaluations of agent-driven analyses through the use of blind analysis and injection tests, which are critical in a t

pa:2611.29590.name: KernelShift: Benchmarking Kernel Optimization Across Evolving Hardware
pa:2611.29590.desc: A benchmarking pipeline evaluates coding agents on optimizing CPU kernels across evolving Arm architectural extensions, showing strong gains on established SIMD extensions but unreliable adaptation to newer matrix-tile programming models.

pa:2611.31239.name: Lyris: Layout-Guided Long Video Generation with Persistent 3D Memory
pa:2611.31239.desc: Lyris uses persistent point-cloud memory and vision-language-model-authored 3D layouts to generate long, camera-controlled walkthroughs from a single photo, improving camera accuracy and return consistency.

pa:2611.30254.name: Innata-0: A Native Embodied World System with Model-Agent Co-Design
pa:2611.30254.desc: Innata-0 is a native embodied world system that co-designs a world-action model and an agent to enable reliable long-horizon physical behaviors through integrated understanding, prediction, action generation, memory, verification, and recovery.

hf:prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-2.5-27B-GGUF.name: prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-2.5-27B-GGUF
hf:prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-2.5-27B-GGUF.zh: 採用三元權重技術的 27B 語言模型，旨在降低推論時的記憶體佔用與運算需求

pa:2611.32067.name: LoopDVR: Looped Transformer for Efficient Dense Visual Recognition
pa:2611.32067.desc: LoopDVR converts pretrained Transformer-based dense visual recognition models into parameter-efficient looped networks by selectively reusing Transformer blocks with adapters, reducing parameters while preserving accuracy.
pa:2611.32067.org: GVC Lab at Great Bay University

pa:2611.32554.name: PartAgent: Agentic 3D Part Segmentation via Expert Integration and Closed-Loop Refinement
pa:2611.32554.desc: A training-free agentic framework integrates pretrained 3D and 2D experts with closed-loop refinement to achieve state-of-the-art 3D part segmentation across multiple benchmarks.
pa:2611.32554.org: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

pa:2611.29547.name: Align the Pair, Not the Sample: Representation Alignment for Faster and Better One-Step Generato
pa:2611.29547.desc: In one-step generator training, aligning the paired reconstruction path rather than the generative path improves recall and sample quality while accelerating both training stages and lowering FID.

pa:2611.31184.name: On-Policy Codec Distillation for Efficient All-in-One Video Generation
pa:2611.31184.desc: Modern visual generative models operate on tokens, and every visual asset they receive, whether an identity, a scribble, a depth map, or a motion video, is tokenized and appended to the input token sequence. Consequently, conditioning quickly dominates the computation cost. Yet most of these tokens carry redundant spatiotemporal information. Our key insight is that identifying what is genuinely ne

pa:2611.30962.name: Self-Evolving Evaluation Environments for Computer-Use Agents
pa:2611.30962.desc: CUA-SEE is a closed-loop evaluation environment that co-evolves tasks and executable verifiers to adaptively measure computer-use agents’ capabilities, boundaries, and progress reliability.

pa:2611.32094.name: Clinical3D-Bench: Evaluating and Improving Spatial Intelligence of Multimodal LLMs in Hospital Environments
pa:2611.32094.desc: A simulated hospital benchmark shows that multimodal large language models have limited spatial reasoning, while fine-tuning and a 3D-computation method improve their accuracy and reduce the gap to physicians.

pa:2611.31205.name: ACAP: Asynchronous Coding Agents for Efficient Robot Control
pa:2611.31205.desc: Coding agents can construct and revise robot behavior during execution, but using one agent for the whole robot can delay otherwise independent work. We introduce Asynchronous Coding Agents as Policy (ACAP), an asynchronous framework that organizes one robot as a team of persistent agents. Each member reasons and acts for a configurable control group, such as an arm with its gripper or the torso a
pa:2611.31205.zh: 用多工分工團隊讓機器人反應更靈敏
pa:2611.31205.why: 把機器人拆成多個獨立AI同時幫忙寫程式與調整動作，解決單一AI忙不過來的情形

pa:2611.28719.name: KMed-31B Technical Report
pa:2611.28719.desc: We present KMed-31B, a medical large language model post-trained from an open-weight model for on-premises deployment with limited hardware. Post-training a model for diverse medical tasks remains difficult, because improving one kind of task can lower performance on another. We attribute this to differences between tasks in expected output and available feedback. Medical question answering and di

pa:2611.25848.name: Interpretable Prototype-Conditioned Adaptation for Weather Forecasting
pa:2611.25848.desc: Group-specific prototype banks with cross-variable attention and sparse low-rank corrections improve the accuracy and interpretability of neural weather forecasting by explicitly linking local prototype contributions to prediction errors.

pa:2611.28947.name: Don't Sleep, Keep Watch: Proactive Perception for Computer-Use Agents
pa:2611.28947.desc: NightWatch adds a lightweight streaming watcher to vision-language computer-use agents to keep perception synchronized with dynamic interfaces, reducing latency and wasted time while maintaining or improving task success.
pa:2611.28947.zh: 幫電腦操作助理加裝即時監控眼
pa:2611.28947.why: 讓AI盯著常變動的電腦畫面，減少發呆等候的時間，做事更快更順暢

pa:2611.30634.name: Rewirable Circuits in Transformers with Loom Attention
pa:2611.30634.desc: We propose loom attention, which allows a Transformer to dynamically rewire its circuits at every token by interweaving a head's vertical attention over the outputs of earlier heads (to obtain its query, key and value) with its horizontal attention over tokens. We instantiate vertical attention efficiently with normalized and gated linear attention over a per-token matrix memory, which stores the
pa:2611.30634.zh: 讓AI在運作時能動態調整思考結構
pa:2611.30634.why: 突破傳統AI固定的運作方式，讓模型能根據不同狀況隨時改變內部連結，處理複雜任務更靈活

pa:2611.29150.name: Can an Agent Trust Its Own Zoom? Cross-Magnification Provenance Verification for Whole-Slide Images
pa:2611.29150.desc: Visual agents navigate whole-slide images through magnified observations associated with claimed locations. However, a visually plausible observation does not necessarily originate from its claimed location, particularly across magnifications and in regions with similar tissue structures. We formulate cross-magnification provenance verification (CMPV) to evaluate whether visual evidence supports a

pa:2611.32100.name: EEGJev: A System One Decision Model and Benchmark for Multi-Task EEG Question Answering
pa:2611.32100.desc: A single electroencephalographic (EEG) recording can support multiple decoding tasks. Fixed-label tests cannot show how EEG foundation models handle changing questions or options. We introduce EEGJev, a fast decision model that scores candidate answers in one pass. Our benchmark, EEGJev-Bench, covers six question types across 19 public EEG sources. We held the recording and options fixed while swi

pa:2611.25403.name: Antom 3-in-1 Transformer: A Payment Foundation Model
pa:2611.25403.desc: We report the development of Antom 3-in-1 Transformer, a payment foundation model that integrates sequence, tabular, and graph representations for payment risk detection. The model contains approximately 7B parameters, with approximately 1.7B activated per task route. Antom 3-in-1 Transformer is pretrained to learn reusable behavioral and relational representations, primarily on Ant International'
pa:2611.25403.zh: 結合三種資料的支付防詐AI模型
pa:2611.25403.why: 把交易流程、表格數據與關聯網路整合在一起，能在龐大支付中更準確抓出詐騙風險

pa:2611.29874.name: Escriba-OCR: A 1B Vision-Language Model for Error-Preserving Transcription of Handwritten Portuguese Essays
pa:2611.29874.desc: Feedback tools and research on learner writing need transcriptions of handwritten essays that keep exactly what the student wrote: misspellings, line breaks, struck-through words and insertions. Vision-language models (VLMs) read handwriting well, but they also tend to rewrite it into correct language. We measure this on BRESSAY, 1,000 handwritten Brazilian Portuguese essays, with a benchmark that

pa:2611.29184.name: PhyCoVE: Benchmarking Physical Counterfactual Video Editing across Diverse Material Dynamics
pa:2611.29184.desc: PhyCoVE, a 533-case benchmark, and counterfactual fidelity evaluate video editing models on physical counterfactual edits involving rigid, elastic, and fluid dynamics, showing that even the best model reproduces only about one seventh of the physical change.

pa:2611.28649.name: S-Mind: Internalizing Multi-View Geometry for Spatial Intelligence
pa:2611.28649.desc: Spatial intelligence, the ability to reason about 3D space from visual observations, becomes essential as multimodal large language models (MLLMs) move into the physical world. Beyond perceiving each view, it rests on two cornerstones of human cognition: fusing multiple views into one coherent 3D scene and mentally transforming that scene to new viewpoints as reasoning unfolds. Yet our spatial pro

pa:2611.25595.name: LoopedWAM: Looped World Action Models for Elastic Inference
pa:2611.25595.desc: World action models (WAMs) couple generative video modeling with robotic action prediction but typically require large video and action transformers, limiting deployment efficiency. We present LoopedWAM, a compact WAM that recurrently applies a shared six-block core in each expert, executing 30 transformer layers while storing only 12 blocks per expert. To account for their asymmetric inference co
pa:2611.25595.org: Center for Research in Computer Vision, University of Central Florida

pa:2611.30219.name: RoomTokens: Masked Diffusion over Structured Tokens for Indoor Scene Synthesis
pa:2611.30219.desc: Generating 3D indoor scenes requires a representation that captures object semantics, instance identity, height structure, and orientation while respecting room geometry. pa:2611.30149.name: LeadVLA: Learning Follower-Aware Route Execution for Robot Leading
pa:2611.30149.desc: LeadVLA is a structured multimodal policy that separates route execution into explicit path, pace, and residual components, trained and evaluated with generated closed-loop data and a benchmark, achieving the highest success among tested robot policies and transferring to unseen real environments without fine-tuning.

pa:2611.28574.name: EvoViM: Recursively Self-Evolving Visual Agents for Exploration with Deferred Queries
pa:2611.28574.desc: EvoViM lets frozen multimodal agents recursively evolve a pixel-level visual program from interaction experience, improving deferred-query visual reasoning and sequential decision-making over strong baselines.

pa:2611.31595.name: LUCID: Statistically Grounded Self-Correction for LLM Reasoning Evaluation
pa:2611.31595.desc: LUCID calibrates language-model step ratings using prompt-based self-correction and Design-based Supervised Learning, reducing bias and improving reasoning audit and selection accuracy without retraining.

pa:2611.30075.name: Context-Grounded Skill Internalization for Vision-Language Agents
pa:2611.30075.desc: Context-Grounded Skill Internalization mitigates context misalignment in skill-removed fine-tuning by detecting and masking or rewriting unsupported skill references, preserving task success while reducing training and processing costs.

pa:2611.31358.name: Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation
pa:2611.31358.desc: Visual creation demands expressive imagery together with precise control over text, layout, and structure. We introduce Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation, an agentic framework that connects these capabilities through Pixel as Code. Raster images are represented by learned discrete visual tokens, while structured artifacts use explicit programs. A shared generation-and-rendering interface connects these

pa:2611.31237.name: Let Vision-Language Models Generate Images through Their Representations
pa:2611.31237.desc: Integral converts a pretrained vision-language model into a unified multimodal model by constructing a shared visual representation space, preserving understanding while enabling strong visual generation.

pa:2611.30235.name: PixelOne: From Options to Pixels in a Single Forward for GUI Grounding
pa:2611.30235.desc: PixelOne transfers spatial knowledge from a search teacher to a student to predict GUI clicks at native resolution in one forward pass, achieving high accuracy and low latency.

pa:2611.32918.name: InstructReplay: Replaying Assistant Turns to Preserve General Behavior During Factual Fine-Tuning
pa:2611.32918.desc: InstructReplay preserves an instruction-tuned language model's general abilities during fact fine-tuning by keeping its responses close to the initial model's answers on general instructions, reducing benchmark decline while still learning new facts.

pa:2611.31258.name: RECAP: Training Long-horizon LLM Agents with Context Compaction
pa:2611.31258.desc: A reinforcement learning framework, RECAP, optimizes context compaction by aligning compressed-context behavior with original-history behavior, improving long-horizon agent performance.

pa:2611.30963.name: Foresight Forcing: Learning Spatial Foresight for Robotic Manipulation
pa:2611.30963.desc: Foresight Forcing distills geometry-aware spatial transition queries from a frozen 3D foundation model to improve robotic manipulation action prediction without requiring future observations at deployment.

pa:2611.33148.name: CoT-Proxy: Cross-Format Transfer for Distilling Long-Horizon Policies
pa:2611.33148.desc: Reasoning models become long-horizon agents through reinforcement learning or, more cheaply, through fine-tuning on a stronger teacher's trajectories, which contain the teacher's chain-of-thought as well as its actions. pa:2611.31442.name: Small Learned Projections for Semantic-Reversal-Aware Retrieval with Spectral Acceleration: A Four-Domain Empirical Study
pa:2611.31442.desc: Dense-embedding retrievers can fail adversarially: when a query is answered by a document A and reversed by a near-copy B that differs from A by a small meaning-changing edit (a "trap"), raw cosine over E5-Large-v2 places B in the top-10 for 82-100% of queries at a pool of 5,000. pa:2611.33020.name: GRAPE-Bench: When Vision Degrades, Does Video Reasoning Hold?
pa:2611.33020.desc: GRAPE-Bench jointly evaluates video reasoning under visual degradation and question difficulty, exposing model weaknesses and enabling improvement and control.

pa:2611.32973.name: SpecEngineeringBench: Evaluating Coding Agents as Autonomous Specification Engineers
pa:2611.32973.desc: Autonomous specification engineering requires coding agents to translate functional requirements into executable tests and use the results to discover and validate defects. pa:2611.32639.name: ReFocus: Progress-Guided Adaptive Practice for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation Reinforcement Learning
pa:2611.32639.desc: ReFocus alternates global and local reinforcement learning with DAG-based progress rewards and adaptive practice windows to target task bottlenecks, improving long-horizon manipulation success over a π0.5 baseline.

pa:2611.32884.name: Lazy Agents Answer Against Their Own Beliefs: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Beliefs Teaches Them to Act on What They Believe
pa:2611.32884.desc: A reinforcement learning method rewards agents for delaying commitment until their inferred posterior over answers is sufficiently narrow, improving evidence-based answering across vision-language benchmarks.
