pa:2611.25509.name: LingSante MedGuard Technical Report
pa:2611.25509.desc: As medical AI is increasingly used for patient consultation and clinical decision support, identifying harmful, non-compliant, or ethically problematic responses is essential for responsible deployment. Assessing these risks requires checking clinical claims against relevant evidence, verifying calculations, and applying medical requirements under their intended conditions. We introduce LingSante

pa:2611.33010.name: Embodied AI Fails the Mirror Test: How a Simple Mirror Breaks Robot Policies
pa:2611.33010.desc: A new benchmark shows that many robot manipulation policies perform worse when mirrors are present, often because they confuse reflections with real objects rather than simply colliding with the mirror.

pa:2611.32423.name: Factorized Context Attention: From Emulated to Native Grid Probing
pa:2611.32423.desc: Factorized Context Attention is a training-free block-sparse attention method that natively reproduces grid probing’s span-based attention pattern, encoding input once into a KV cache to match accuracy and extend context at lower cost across video, text, and image tasks.
pa:2611.32423.org: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology

pa:2611.32617.name: VenusOCR2.0: Towards Efficient and Effective Document Parsing
pa:2611.32617.desc: We present VenusOCR2.0, a compact 1B-parameter vision-language recognizer designed for both high-accuracy and high-throughput document parsing across text, tables, and formulas. To continuously improve recognition quality without self-training collapse, we build a bounded recursive self-improvement (RSI) data engine where the model acts strictly as a weakness probe, while external multi-expert med

pa:2611.30986.name: Reinforcing Diffusion Models by Instantaneous Trajectory Distribution Matching
pa:2611.30986.desc: Forward diffusion reinforcement learning (RL)---enabling deterministic ODE sampling without trajectory backpropagation---has grown increasingly popular for efficiently aligning diffusion models. However, we reveal that existing methods essentially rely on signed reward-weighted regression (RWR), regressing the trainable policy velocity onto rollouts from a behavior distribution. Unbiased baseline

pa:2611.32183.name: ThinkMorph-SSL: Scaling Interleaved Multimodal Reasoning with Pretext Tasks
pa:2611.32183.desc: A two-stage training approach uses visual pretext tasks to generate interleaved image-text reasoning traces and automatically built demonstrations, improving multimodal reasoning over instruction tuning alone.

pa:2611.31466.name: AdProducer: Towards Agentic Advertising Video Generation
pa:2611.31466.desc: An end-to-end multimodal agent framework autonomously researches products and creates selling-point-driven storyboards to guide a frozen video generator, trained via supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning to produce effective advertising videos.

pa:2611.32736.name: Qwen-Image-HD: Autoregressive Diffusion for High Definition Image Generation
pa:2611.32736.desc: Fine-tuning a generator on a complete high-resolution canvas requires long image sequences and substantial computation, yet local regions can still exhibit unnatural repetitive stripes when training resources are limited. pa:2611.32820.name: Residual Guidance for Real-Time Interactive Video Generation
pa:2611.32820.desc: Residual Guidance is a training-free method that counteracts context inertia in streaming video generation by adding a residual from denoising the previous chunk under the new prompt to early denoising steps, improving prompt switching without training or per-model tuning.

pa:2611.31766.name: RoMo Hands: A Large Scale Richly Organized Text to Hand Motion Dataset
pa:2611.31766.desc: A large-scale text-paired dataset of bimanual hand motion, paired with a 393-D representation and benchmark, enables systematic evaluation of generative models for dexterous motion synthesis.

pa:2611.32462.name: MAGPIE: Agentic Multi-Reference Image Generation via Executable Scene Construction
pa:2611.32462.desc: Multi-reference image generation requires a model to preserve the appearance of selected subjects while arranging them according to an instruction. Despite recent progress in reference-based generation and compositional control, reliably organizing selected subjects into the intended scene remains challenging. Although existing methods provide various forms of compositional guidance, the planned r

pa:2611.30488.name: Do learned image captioning metrics generalize? Auditing duplicated samples in human-judgment benchmarks
pa:2611.30488.desc: An audit of recent image captioning evaluation benchmarks shows that duplicate samples and metric behavior inflate reported correlations, and proposes a protocol under which zero-shot vision-language judges perform best on recent test sets.

pa:2611.31974.name: Coding4Games: Can Modern Coding Agents Play Modern Video Games?
pa:2611.31974.desc: Games, especially modern AAA games, challenge language models to perceive complex scenes, control actions, and make decisions over long horizons. Existing game benchmarks primarily test language models as computer-use agents that query a language model throughout play, incurring repeated inference cost and, in real-time games, acting while the environment continues to evolve. We ask whether coding

pa:2611.29389.name: PINE: Point, Instance and Normal Estimation in One-Step Diffusion Model
pa:2611.29389.desc: Understanding a scene requires both geometry and semantics: geometry recovers its spatial structure, and semantics separates it into objects. Current models obtain the two from separate networks or separate passes. pa:2611.32816.name: SpatialArena: Where Do Geometric Foundation Models Stand?
pa:2611.32816.desc: SpatialArena is an open benchmark that evaluates geometric models across five 3D perception tasks using uniform metrics and robust alignment, revealing that single-image depth is near saturation on public benchmarks but progress now depends on cross-frame and cross-view consistency.

pa:2510.22622.name: Mega-MMDF and DeepfakeBench-MM: Benchmarking Multimodal Deepfake Detection Across Diverse Forgery Pipelines
pa:2510.22622.desc: A large audio-visual deepfake benchmark and standardized evaluation suite show that diverse composite-forgery training improves detection performance but does not reliably generalize to constituent manipulations, while modality masking and temporal misalignment increase detection errors.

pa:2611.31977.name: Distill to Loop: Turning Pretrained Diffusion Transformers into Looped Models with Adjustable Depth
pa:2611.31977.desc: A pretrained diffusion transformer is distilled into a weight-shared looped student that supports variable loop counts at inference and uses depth-wise ODE solvers and loop guidance to match teacher quality with fewer parameters and less compute.
pa:2611.31977.org: Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University

pa:2611.31752.name: Separating Measurement Failures from Defence Failures in Split Language-Model Privacy
pa:2611.31752.desc: Split-training privacy evaluations fail through distinct mechanisms. Evaluators can overlook an exposed gradient channel, align reconstructions against shifted labels, or deploy uncalibrated probes before testing a candidate defence, while calibrated attacks can also refute real defences. Separating these failure modes alters which claims survive. We conduct a retrospective evidentiary reanalysis

pa:2611.32782.name: Measuring Layer-wise Intrinsic Dimensionality of FFNs in LLMs via PCA
pa:2611.32782.desc: Large language models exhibit a middle-heavy intrinsic-dimensionality profile in their feed-forward layers, and using this profile to guide width allocation improves pruning under a fixed parameter budget.

pa:2611.32649.name: ICLWorld: Benchmarking In-Context Learning of Agents from Digital to Physical Worlds
pa:2611.32649.desc: An online benchmark evaluates in-context learning across computer-use and robot-use agent tasks, revealing large gaps between digital and physical performance and between recognizing rules and acting on them.

pa:2611.31129.name: FATCAT: Fault Injection Attacks Targeting Chip-level Alignment
pa:2611.31129.desc: Model alignment is the primary safety and security mechanism for enforcing refusal of malicious prompts in modern foundation models; yet, existing adversarial evaluations implicitly assume underlying hardware integrity. pa:2611.32393.name: Fractal Neural Synthesis: Constant-Storage Procedural Weight Derivation via Complex Quadratic Boundary Dynamics
pa:2611.32393.desc: Conventional neural networks store synaptic parameters as explicit tensors whose persistent Flash footprint scales linearly (O(W)) with parameter count, constraining resource-limited edge microcontrollers. pa:2611.25946.name: Point Dynamics as Proxy for Robotic World Models
pa:2611.25946.desc: Separating dynamics prediction from visual rendering using 3D point dynamics as an intermediate representation improves object motion accuracy in robotic video world models without sacrificing image quality.

pa:2611.27404.name: Degradation of Language Models under Controlled Load: Synchronization, Rule Execution and Misfires on the Background
pa:2611.27404.desc: A method separates a language model's quality decline under controlled load into synchronization, rule execution, and misfires, then derives load-dependent laws that characterize each model.

pa:2611.30017.name: OWE-Bench: A long-horizon benchmark for measuring real-world engineering
pa:2611.30017.desc: We present OWE-Bench (OpenWorldEngineer-Bench), a benchmark of 26 long-horizon engineering tasks written by domain experts in software engineering, physical engineering, machine learning, and scientific computing. pa:2611.33636.name: What Is Redundant at High Resolution? Efficient Attention and Feed-Forward Design for All-in-One Image Restoration
pa:2611.33636.desc: A multi-scale image restoration network reduces redundant computation in attention and feed-forward layers to achieve state-of-the-art restoration with faster inference.

pa:2611.34575.name: Sage-Med: Scaling Medical Multimodal Intelligence
pa:2611.34575.desc: Establishing effective scaling laws for medical multimodal large language models (MLLMs) remains a persistent and fundamental challenge. pa:2611.34237.name: VibeVideoAgent: Closing the Perceptual Loop for Code-Driven Video Generation
pa:2611.34237.desc: Code-driven video generation asks a coding agent to write and run rendering programs. This gives exact control over typography, data visualizations, synchronized audio, and multi-shot scenes, and it leaves an editable project behind. pa:2611.34907.name: Agentic LongLive: Asynchronous Agentic Memory for Long Video Generation
pa:2611.34907.desc: Real-time autoregressive video generators stream minutes of video and accept new prompts on the fly, but struggle to keep people, objects, and places consistent over a long interactive story. pa:2611.28010.name: Beyond Code and Pixels: Co-Generating Editable and Visually Rich Presentations
pa:2611.28010.desc: SlidesWeaver combines language and vision agents with diffusion-based planning and shared state to generate editable, high-quality PPTX presentations while preserving native text and layout.

pa:2611.31895.name: Loupe: Reinforcing Knowledge-Intensive Video Generation Agents
pa:2611.31895.desc: Knowledge-intensive video generation remains challenging because prompts often omit the facts, appearances, and temporal relationships required for accurate generation. pa:2611.30460.name: CONCOR: Benchmarking Contrastive Decoding for Visual Hallucination Mitigation Beyond Final-Output Performance
pa:2611.30460.desc: A controlled benchmark directly evaluates contrastive corrections in multimodal large language models to better understand and mitigate object hallucination beyond final task scores.

pa:2611.30472.name: Target-Part Preference Optimization for Part-Aware 3D Generation
pa:2611.30472.desc: Preference fine-tuning based on Direct Preference Optimization adapts a pretrained part-aware 3D generator with limited part annotations, yielding the best multi-part results at medium scale but less consistent gains under distribution shift.

pa:2611.33915.name: SEEK: Self-Evolution through Execution Knowledge for Agentic Robot Manipulation
pa:2611.33915.desc: SEEK retains executable manipulation procedures and measured action effects across attempts, enabling fixed foundation-model robots to improve without retraining.

pa:2611.33143.name: ROAM-Bench: Evaluating Embodied Active Spatial Intelligence through Evidence Verification
pa:2611.33143.desc: Embodied spatial intelligence requires agents to gather information through exploration and interaction, then use it to reason and act. Existing benchmarks insufficiently distinguish correct outcomes from completion of these task requirements. We introduce ROAM-Bench to evaluate these abilities under robot motion and collision constraints. Independent checks use simulation state and episode record

pa:2611.33144.name: PyRUA-Dex: Learning Programmatic Policies for Dexterous Bimanual Manipulation with Coding Agents
pa:2611.33144.desc: A framework enables coding agents to develop dexterous manipulation policies without demonstrations by exploring and distilling successful attempts into a program, then refining it for strong simulated and real-world results.

pa:2611.30844.name: DyLoMo-DiT: Dynamic Looped Mixture-of-Experts Diffusion Transformers
pa:2611.30844.desc: A dynamic looped mixture-of-experts diffusion transformer reuses shared parameters and varies compute across noise levels, improving image generation quality under matched budgets.

pa:2611.27962.name: Model Carving: Training Transformers That Optimize Their Own Topology
pa:2611.27962.desc: Model Carving jointly learns a Transformer's weights and architecture by gating sublayers during training, producing smaller, faster, and stronger models than dense, pruned, or distilled alternatives.

pa:2611.32199.name: Steerable by Design: Conditional Pretraining for Robust Control of Language Models
pa:2611.32199.desc: Our goal is to build language models that are steerable by design. Today's language models are pretrained with next-token prediction, which relegates alignment and control to the final 1% of training tokens or inference-time interventions. pa:2611.32351.name: LookAnything: A Foundation Model for Holistic Gaze Following
pa:2611.32351.desc: Human gaze provides a rich window into attention and intent, making its understanding essential for applications ranging from social signal analysis to human-robot interaction. Existing methods typically employ highly customized architectures relying on auxiliary inputs like head crops or depth maps, causing cascading errors and inference overhead. Trained on single domains and confined to isolate

pa:2611.30564.name: Seeing Is Locating: Spatial Awareness and Geographic Bias in Decision Language Models
pa:2611.30564.desc: A multimodal benchmark evaluates decision models on spatial awareness and geographic bias across image classification and location rating tasks, revealing reliance on vision and socioeconomic biases, and proposes a training-free location-prior method to improve spatial awareness.

pa:2611.21056.name: Evaluation-Free Recursive Self-Improvement for Coding Agents
pa:2611.21056.desc: ELITE enables coding agents to self-improve by integrating complementary implementation mechanisms from independently generated improvements without using downstream task evaluations in the evolution loop, achieving strong SWE-bench performance and transfer.

pa:2611.34147.name: Letting Models Manage Their Own Context: Where We Stand
pa:2611.34147.desc: Model-driven context management through a context API improves accuracy and token efficiency over harness-triggered compaction, while reusing KV caches after edits reduces prefill compute.

pa:2611.32786.name: Simulator-as-Proxy World Model for Robot Manipulation
pa:2611.32786.desc: SimPWM uses a parameter-free simulator as a proxy to generate robot videos and simulated states, revealing that video models follow arm motion more reliably than object dynamics and often ignore simulated object state.

pa:2611.33307.name: Lost in Translation, Not in Confidence: Benchmarking and Calibrating Multilingual Decision Models
pa:2611.33307.desc: Decision models are language models fine-tuned to return a probability for each option of a typed query, which routers and guardrails threshold directly. They are built on multilingual bases but ranked almost entirely in English. pa:2611.34777.name: When Every Rollout Fails: Splicing Learner-Conditioned Options into Long-Horizon Agent RL
pa:2611.34777.desc: SPLICE improves reinforcement learning on long-horizon agent tasks by constructing local training targets from failed trajectories using a proposal model to select splice points and generate bounded options, outperforming GRPO and full-trajectory guidance baselines.

pa:2611.34756.name: Collect for Coverage, Replay with Evidence: Adaptive and Efficient On-Policy Distillation for Long-Horizon Agents
pa:2611.34756.desc: Fully online on-policy distillation (OPD) is costly for long-horizon agents because each update depends on fresh environment rollouts. Prefix replay offers an efficient alternative by sampling current-student responses from stored histories, reducing idle time for long-tail rollouts and allowing each collected trajectory to support multiple updates. pa:2611.34939.name: A Mesh for Every Moment
pa:2611.34939.desc: We present MEMO (a Mesh for Every MOment), a method that reconstructs the geometry of complete dynamic scenes, captured by multiple synchronized cameras, and extracts a mesh at every frame. pa:2611.33579.name: DexEngine: Scaling Human Demonstrations into Physically Executable Whole-Robot Data
pa:2611.33579.desc: A growing body of recent work addresses the retargeting of human hand-object demonstrations to robotic hands. To train whole-robot policies, however, the retargeted motions must be kinematically feasible and physically executable, and be produced efficiently at scale. pa:2611.34671.name: DemoFoundry: Toward Scalable Photorealistic Robot Data with Coding Agents and Generative Rendering
pa:2611.34671.desc: Scaling robot learning requires demonstrations that combine realistic visual observations with reliable action supervision. We present DemoFoundry, an automated framework that couples coding

pa:2611.30895.name: Speak When You See It: Proactive Task Assistants Should Wait for Evidence, Not the Clock
pa:2611.30895.desc: Proactive assistants that guide people through physical tasks must decide, every few seconds, whether a step is complete and whether a mistake has occurred. pa:2611.34750.name: SOLVE: Sparse, Ordered Keyposes Make LLM Agents Versatile and Efficient Robot Manipulator
pa:2611.34750.desc: LLM agents have made remarkable progress in robot manipulation, yet they suffer from expensive inference, dense step-by-step control, and tool bottlenecks. pa:2611.32002.name: Change the Base, Change the Game: Rethinking Pan-sharpening
pa:2611.32002.desc: Many pan-sharpening (PS) networks reconstruct high-resolution multispectral (HRMS) images by adding learned residuals to 4times-interpolated low-resolution multispectral (LRMS) inputs, incorporating panchromatic (PAN) detail only through these residual corrections. pa:2611.33457.name: Playfulness as Feedback for Agentic Game Development
pa:2611.33457.desc: Play2Evolve uses AI agents to iteratively playtest, diagnose, and improve generated games through initialization, refinement, and evolution stages, enhancing functionality, visuals, and gameplay quality.

pa:2611.34420.name: DocSEAM: Bidirectional Cross-Page Encoding for Multi-Page Document Understanding
pa:2611.34420.desc: DocSEAM is a lightweight module between a pretrained vision encoder and language model that enriches page visual tokens with neighboring-page context via center-anchored masked self-attention, improving multi-page document VQA and reducing boundary sensitivity.

pa:2611.34923.name: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer
pa:2611.34923.desc: A Mixture-of-Loops Transformer reuses key-value memory across loops and depths, and its U-shaped variant improves pretraining efficiency and inference latency.

pa:2611.33925.name: Beyond the Happy Path: Generalizing Robot World Models from Simulated Failures
pa:2611.33925.desc: Training world models on simulated manipulation failures with interaction alignment and surface correspondence reduces object trajectory and action-outcome prediction errors, including on unseen objects and real data.

pa:2611.34064.name: SPARC: Geometry-Guided Attention Pruning for Long-Horizon Camera-Controlled Video Generation
pa:2611.34064.desc: SPARC uses geometry-guided pruning of self-attention in pretrained video diffusion transformers to unify camera control and persistent scene memory, improving camera adherence and revisit consistency while greatly reducing computation.

pa:2611.34912.name: LiveVAE: Causal Window Attention Makes Efficient Streaming Video VAE
pa:2611.34912.desc: While video diffusion models have grown faster and increasingly streamable, the video VAE remains a primary latency bottleneck across interactive generation and editing pipelines. pa:2611.34466.name: EgoUseBench: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents under Evolving First-Person Contexts
pa:2611.34466.desc: AI wearables, such as smart glasses, extend the context available to agents beyond digital environments to users' physical surroundings. With these devices, computer tasks can originate from users' ongoing activities rather than solely from explicit instructions. pa:2611.32473.name: OmniPersist: Persistent Dynamic World Modeling via Coupled Panoramic Evolution
pa:2611.32473.desc: Action-conditioned world models play a vital role in robotics and autonomous driving, yet existing video diffusion models struggle to maintain dynamic object persistence. pa:2611.34929.name: High-Fidelity Image Matting with Pixel-Space Diffusion Transformers
pa:2611.34929.desc: Diffusion models have shown strong potential for image matting by transferring generative priors learned from large-scale pretraining.
